title: Telescopes & Observatories
tagline: Ways we learned to see further.
source: Generated from “Timeline of telescopes, observatories, and observing technology” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.
wikiPage: Timeline of telescopes, observatories, and observing technology

events.title: Infrared Astronomical Satellite
events.text: Infrared Astronomical Satellite (IRAS) telescope

events.title: IRAM 30-m
events.text: IRAM 30-m telescope at Pico Veleta near Granada, Spain completed

events.title: James Clerk Maxwell Telescope
events.text: m James Clerk Maxwell Telescope UK submillimetre telescope installed at Mauna Kea Observatory

events.title: La Silla Observatory
events.text: m Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope (SEST) installed at the ESO La Silla Observatory

events.title: Cambridge Optical Aperture Synthesis Telescope (COAST)
events.text: Cambridge Optical Aperture Synthesis Telescope (COAST)—the first very high resolution optical astronomical images (from aperture synthesis observations)

events.title: Compton Gamma Ray Observatory
events.text: Compton Gamma Ray Observatory satellite

events.title: VLT
events.text: First light at VLT1, the 8.2 m ESO telescope

events.title: Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope
events.text: Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope of thirty 45 m dishes at Pune

events.title: Hubble
events.text: Hubble 2.4m space Telescope launched, mirror found to be flawed

events.title: Keck 10-meter optical/infrared reflecting telescope
events.text: Keck 10-meter optical/infrared reflecting telescope begins operation, located at Mauna Kea, Hawaii

events.title: Keck 2
events.text: Keck 2 10-meter optical/infrared reflecting telescope begins operation, located at Mauna Kea, Hawaii

events.title: HALCA
events.text: The Japanese HALCA satellite begins operations, producing first VLBI observations from space, 25,000 km maximum baseline

events.title: Very Long Baseline Array
events.text: Very Long Baseline Array of 10 dishes

events.title: Euclid
events.text: Euclid, was launched on 1 July 2023 on a Falcon 9 Block 5 rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida, to study dark matter and energy.

events.title: VLTI
events.text: First imaging with the VLTI using the AMBER optical aperture synthesis instrument and three VLT telescopes.

events.title: Gran Telescopio de Canarias (GTC)
events.text: First light at Gran Telescopio de Canarias (GTC), in Spain, the largest optical telescope in the world with an effective diameter of 10.4 meters.

events.title: SALT
events.text: First light at SALT, the largest optical telescope in the Southern Hemisphere, with a hexagonal primary mirror of 11.1 by 9.8 meters.

events.title: Keck Interferometer
events.text: First light at the Keck Interferometer. Single-baseline operations begin in the near-infrared.

events.title: VLTI
events.text: First light at VLTI interferometry array. Operations on the interferometer start with single-baseline near-infrared observations with the 103 m baseline.

events.title: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
events.text: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), was launched 25 December 2021 on an ESA Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana and will succeed the Hubble Space Telescope as NASA's flagship mission in astrophysics.

events.title: XRISM
events.text: XRISM was launched on 6 September 2023 on a H-IIA rocket to study the formation of the universe and the dark matter.

events.title: Public Telescope (PST)
events.text: Public Telescope (PST), German project of astrofactum. Launch was planned for 2019, but the project's website is now defunct and no updates have been provided on the fate of the effort.

events.title: Iranian National Observatory
events.text: Iranian National Observatory 3.4 m (first light planned in 2020)

events.title: Vera C. Rubin Observatory
events.text: Mid/late-2021 – Science first light of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory is anticipated for 2021 with full science operations to begin a year later.

events.title: Extremely Large Telescope
events.text: Extremely Large Telescope (first light planned in 2027)

events.title: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
events.text: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, part of NASA's Exoplanet Exploration Program. Launch is tentatively scheduled for 2027.
